official.deadline_note: No fixed closing date is published. COMSTECH states it 'will accept applications on a yearly basis' and that the 10 fellowships are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to eligibility - so the round effectively closes when the tenth eligible application is received.
official.application_cycle: Yearly intake; applications accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until the 10 places are filled
official.status_note: The official page's Call Status reads 'The call is currently open'.
benefits: COMSTECH will cover, low-cost international airfare and visa fees, if applicable
Host institutions are expected to provide accommodation, subsistence supervision and mentoring of local training
Scholarships are offered for three to six months, extendable upon recommendation from the host institution
eligibility: The fellowship program is open to citizens of all OIC member states, explicitly including the OIC least-developed countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Comoros, Djibouti, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Togo, Uganda and Yemen

Applicants must have at least a Bachelor's degree; having Master's or Ph.D. degrees will be an asset. The academic background in food security, agriculture, food science, food safety, or another related field

Applicants with Bachelor's degrees must have at least 5 years of substantive professional experience, preferably in government or national research institutions after university graduation. For applicants with a Master's or Ph.D., at least 3 years of professional experience, preferably in a government or national research institution
Fluent and proficient in English, with excellent written and oral communication skills; the fellowship will be conducted in English language
Available full-time (40 hours per week) during the entire duration of the fellowship
Age limit: maximum 35 years (for MS/Ph.D.), 45 years (for Post-Doc)
requirements: The research or training must align with one of the eight published thematic areas
Meet the degree and professional-experience threshold for your qualification level
Demonstrate fluency in English; the fellowship is conducted in English
Be available full-time, 40 hours per week, for the entire duration
Be within the age limit for your level
Note on the application form: applications or supporting documents submitted in French will not be considered for evaluation
documents: Completed official COMSTECH application form (submitted through the linked JotForm)
Clear scan of degree / transcript (PDF or JPG, file size must not exceed 300kb)
Scan of one recommendation letter from the current/most recent institution (PDF or JPG, max 300kb)
Clear scan of passport (PDF or JPG, max 300kb)
Detailed CV enlisting all educational/professional activities, research publications and a clear picture, from not more than 6 months ago (PDF only, max 500kb)
Two written statements of at least 200 words each: why you want this fellowship and why you are a good fit, and your detailed research/training objectives
selection_criteria: Only 10 fellowships are available and will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to eligibility
Research fellowships are awarded by OIC-COMSTECH, as well as by the Joint Scholarship Committee of the host institutions, based on scientific merit
COMSTECH will accept applications on a yearly basis and select the candidates based on the pre-approved selection criteria
coverage: Visa fees, if applicable (covered by COMSTECH)
Supervision and mentoring of local training
application_method: Review the eight thematic areas and choose the one your proposed research aligns with
Review the list of CCoE member institutions and select up to two preferred host institutions (placement preference is not guaranteed)
Complete the official application form (JotForm) with all required uploads attached
Applications are considered on a first-come, first-served basis until the 10 available places are filled
official.application_route: Single online application via the official COMSTECH JotForm linked from the fellowship page; no separate application to the host institution is published
official.study_mode: Full-time (40 hours per week) for the entire duration of the fellowship
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of all OIC member states; the OIC least-developed countries explicitly named are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Comoros, Djibouti, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Togo, Uganda and Yemen
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the fellowship is open to citizens of all OIC member states and placements are at various OIC R&D and higher education institutions in other OIC countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Academic background in food security, agriculture, food science, food safety or another related field, with the proposed work matching one of the eight thematic areas (plant biotechnology; human nutrition; the water-food-energy nexus; food science and technology; nutraceuticals/food-medicine continuum; agro-business, trade and food value chains; agricultural technology and innovations; neglected food crops)
official.research_requirement: Applicants must submit a detailed statement of their research/training objectives (at least 200 words on the application form); awards are based on scientific merit
official.duration: 3-6 months, extendable upon recommendation from the host institution
official.description: COMSTECH and CCoE member institutions jointly offer this research fellowship to young researchers in OIC countries, providing short- to medium-term research placements of 3 to 6 months in advanced institutions to build technical capacity in agriculture, food security and related areas. The programme aims to empower early-career professionals by enhancing their research capabilities and fostering long-term collaborations across the OIC scientific community.
official.region: Multiple - citizens of all OIC member states across Africa, the Middle East and Asia; host country is various OIC R&D and Higher Education Institutions
official.program_type: Inter-governmental research fellowship (short- to medium-term research placement under the COMSTECH Consortium of Excellence)
official.english_requirement: Fluent and proficient in English, with excellent written and oral communication skills; the fellowship is conducted in the English language. The application form asks applicants to declare their proficiency level (Not Proficient / Average / Proficient) and states that applications or supporting documents submitted in French will not be considered. No IELTS or TOEFL score is published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an in-kind funded 3-6 month research placement at a COMSTECH Consortium of Excellence institution, not a cash scholarship: COMSTECH pays for low-cost international airfare and visa fees while the host institution provides your accommodation, subsistence and supervision. With only 10 places awarded first-come, first-served and no published closing date, the round can close without warning, so a complete and correctly formatted file beats speed alone. Applications run through one JotForm that demands passport-level personal data, a recent recommendation letter, a CV no older than six months and two 200-word statements, all under strict file-size caps.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers from OIC member states - particularly the named least-developed countries - holding an MS or PhD in nutrition, food science, agriculture or a related field, aged 35 or under, who can take three to six months away from their current post on a full-time basis.
application_readiness_checklist: Compress uploads before you start: degree/transcript, recommendation letter and passport scans must each be 300kb or smaller and in PDF or JPG only; the CV must be a PDF under 500kb
Draft both 200-word statements offline (motivation/fit and detailed research objectives) and map them explicitly onto one of the eight thematic areas
Shortlist up to two CCoE host institutions from the official member list and, ideally, identify a potential supervisor or research group there before submitting
Confirm your passport is valid well beyond the intended placement dates and gather your employment history for the experience check (3 years post-Master's/PhD, 5 years for Bachelor's holders)
Email comstech@comstech.org or Khazima@comstech.org to confirm the call is still open and that places remain before you invest time in the file
common_rejection_risks: All 10 places being filled first-come, first-served before your file is ready - delay is functionally equivalent to rejection on this programme
Uploads rejected for size or format: scans over 300kb (degree/transcript, recommendation letter, passport) or a CV over 500kb or not in PDF
A CV that predates the six-month freshness rule, or a recommendation letter that does not come from your current or most recent institution
A proposal that does not clearly align with one of the eight thematic areas, or an academic background outside food security, agriculture, food science or food safety
Missing the experience threshold for your qualification level, or exceeding the age limit (35 for MS/PhD holders, 45 for post-docs)
Submitting any supporting document in French, which the form states will not be evaluated
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The programme publishes no cash stipend, so personal spending money, local transport around the host city, communications, and any home-country costs (unpaid leave, document attestation, medical checks or travel to a visa appointment) remain on the fellow; accommodation and subsistence are provided by the host institution but are not quantified on the official page, and tuition or enrolment fees are not covered.
document_audit: The three scan uploads (degree/transcript, recommendation letter, passport) are capped at 300kb each and accept only PDF or JPG - phone scans usually need compressing before upload
The CV must be a PDF no larger than 500kb and dated within the last six months, so refresh it immediately before applying
The recommendation letter must come from your current or most recent institution; a letter from a former employer or professor may not satisfy the field

The form collects compulsory personal data including religion, marital status, number of children and previous visits abroad, plus a medical-fitness declaration - assemble these details before opening the form
Documents in French are explicitly not evaluated, so translate everything into English first
The English field is a self-declaration (Not Proficient / Average / Proficient), not an uploaded test certificate, so no IELTS or TOEFL report needs to be attached
alerts: The official page contains internal inconsistencies: the header lists the minimum qualification as MS/Ph.D. while the eligibility text accepts a Bachelor's degree plus five years' experience, and the age-limit line appears twice with different wording ('35 for MS/Ph.D., 45 for post-doc' versus '35 for Master's studies, 45 for doctoral studies') - confirm your specific standing with the secretariat before relying on either reading

There is no published closing date; the single 'The call is currently open' status line plus first-come, first-served allocation means the round can shut at any time once ten eligible applications arrive
Placement at your preferred institution is explicitly not guaranteed even if you list two preferences, so choose preferences where your research genuinely fits the host's capacity
The fellowship demands full-time, 40-hour-per-week availability for the whole 3-6 months, so you need formal leave or a sabbatical arrangement from your current employer before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Assemble and compress all uploads, complete the single COMSTECH JotForm with both 200-word statements and your two host preferences, submit, and then COMSTECH together with the host institutions' Joint Scholarship Committee reviews eligible applications on scientific merit as they arrive until all 10 places are allocated.
